design_note: Distinguish a retry of one accepted business operation from a second legitimate equal-value transaction. The decision tree makes operation identity and parameter matching explicit instead of treating identical amounts as universal duplicate proof.

source.title: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
source.concept: Identical parameters can represent different intended operations. Caller-provided request identities distinguish retries, while a reused identity with changed parameters needs explicit rejection semantics.
source.scope: Original partial-refund domain allows separate approved equal-value refunds. Business operation IDs, balance checks and approval rules are fictional application contracts.

lesson.anchor: Build it: a mutating tool with approval and idempotency
lesson.title: Equal amounts do not always mean the same intent
lesson.intro: PAY-B captured 5000 INR minor units. Approved operation OP-A refunded 1000; OP-B requests another 1000 for a separate accepted return. The fictional service distinguishes authenticated business operation IDs.

yes.label: Return that operation receipt; no new debit

no.label: Reject mismatched reuse of the ID

branches.question: New approval and remaining balance valid?

yes.label: Commit new effect and ID atomically

no.label: No new effect; record unmet gate

read: OP-A identifies one accepted refund even when its response is retried.
OP-B is a distinct operation; its equal amount does not make it OP-A.
A new ID still needs independent authority, approval and sufficient balance.
lesson.question: May OP-B reuse OP-A solely because both requested amounts are 1000 minor units?
lesson.answer: No. OP-A identifies the first return, while OP-B represents a separately accepted return. Returning OP-A would falsely report the second operation as completed. Keep distinct business identities and enforce the remaining balance. Reusing OP-A with changed effect fields must fail parameter matching.
lesson.takeaway: Idempotency identifies an intended operation, not merely similar-looking parameters.
lesson.assumption: Fictional partial-refund contract with authenticated IDs, atomic deduplication and current authority. Two legitimate equal-value refunds are allowed; ordinary gates still apply.
lesson.source_label: AWS: safe retries and intent identity
